get.summary: Liveness — the process is up and serving

get.description: One read for every badge in the product. Answers for whoever is asking, so a client shows the counters its role uses rather than requesting a subset. Always an object, zeroes included — never null.
get.summary: What is waiting on the caller

post.description: Pass threadId to clear one conversation's, or omit it to clear the lot — which is what opening the bell means.

get.description: Three catalogues keyed by audience — an events company, a coach, an advertiser — and no plan belongs to two of them.

post.description: Admins only. A tier is a name, a price, a period and how many events may be live.

get.description: The plan comes from the same function the publish check consults, so this screen and that refusal cannot disagree about which plan somebody is on.

get.summary: What my business has paid for

patch.description: Admins only. Setting maxActiveEvents to 0 on the coach default is what ends the free period for coach events — one edit, no migration.

get.description: Admins only. Newest first.

post.description: Admins only, because only an admin saw the money arrive. Naming an event makes it a per-event purchase, which is a coach paying for one tournament.

get.description: Newest first, cancelled ones included — a withdrawal is part of the record.

post.description: Against a category, which names its own event. Refusals arrive as sentences: the category is full, entries have closed, the age band does not fit.
A family may until the event's cancellation deadline; the organiser may until the event is marked finished. Never a delete — the receipt survives.

patch.description: The organiser's alone. A parent who could set this could mark themselves paid — the same reason a coach does not certify their own trial attendance.

get.description: The owner's register. Anybody else gets an empty list rather than a refusal, because a refusal would confirm the event has entries in it.
Drafts included, soonest first. Declared before the :id route so that /events/mine is not parsed as an event whose id is the word mine.
Published events whose owner is approved and unsuspended. No account needed — a parent deciding whether to sign up should be able to look first.
get.summary: What is on in a city

get.description: Public once published; the owner sees their own drafts too. A draft is a 404 to anybody else, because saying 'forbidden' would confirm it exists.

patch.description: Only fields present in the body are touched. Ownership columns are not editable.

post.description: Always a draft. The owner is taken from the caller's own coach or company row, never from the body — whose event it is is not the client's to nominate.

patch.description: A separate act from editing because publishing has its own condition: the row policy only lets an approved, unsuspended owner move an event to published.

put.description: Send the list the form now shows and it becomes the set. Order of the array is the order they display in, so a client never numbers its own rows.

get.description: Only cities with a live area and at least one approved coach in it, busiest first. The head of this list is the sensible default for a visitor who has not chosen.
Readable signed out. Posts appear here a few hours after they are written, because hiding a reported post needs signed-in reporters and a guest cannot report at all.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return posts older than this. Pass the createdAt of the last post you have.

get.summary: What coaches in a city have been posting

get.description: Posts from coaches they follow, plus coaches in their city teaching what they said they are looking for. Each post carries a `reason` saying which of the two it is.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return posts older than this. Pass the createdAt of the last post you have.

put.description: What /choose-role does on the web, reachable by a client that does not write tables — without it a mobile app can create a session and then has nowhere to go. Settable only while the account has no role; asking for the role you already have returns it. Changing one is a different action and is not always allowed.

Lives on `profiles`, so it is not part of the listing payload — which left a client that does not write tables unable to set it at all. A listing is not complete without one: a coach nobody can ring is a coach nobody books.
put.summary: The number you are reached on

get.description: The first call after signing in. `role: null` means a verified account that has not chosen a role yet — send them to pick one; it is not an error. The seeker or provider block is present only for that role.
get.summary: Who is asking, and what they have finished

get.description: Null before they have created one — a normal state for an account that has picked the role and not filled the form in yet, not an error. Visible while unapproved, so a company waiting on an admin can see what it submitted.

200.description: Null when no listing exists yet.

put.description: One listing per account, so this upserts. Approval and suspension are absent from the body by design and withheld by column privileges besides — naming either is refused by Postgres, not just by this contract.

get.description: 404 for a family who has not filled one in yet. That is the expected state and not an error: the account exists from the moment a role is chosen, and the row is written by the first save.

put.description: The whole profile every time, not a patch: the row is upserted, so a partial payload would clear what it omitted. One call and one transaction — the web does this as an upsert plus a separate profile_complete update.

post.description: The family's direction. A coach approaching a family is POST /students/{kind}/{id}/approach — two inserts into one table under two policies with every clause inverted, so they stay two endpoints.

Accepting opens the conversation; declining closes it. Answers with the thread as it now reads — a declined one included, carrying status `declined`, because that is what a client needs to render the answer.
post.summary: Answer a coach who approached you

delete.description: The coach's side only, and only while it is still pending. The row is deleted rather than marked, because an approach nobody saw is not a conversation that happened.
delete.summary: Take back an approach nobody has answered

put.description: Per enquiry, never per account: sharing a number with one coach is not sharing it with every coach who ever writes. Revocable, and the contact endpoints stop answering the moment it is off.

get.description: `iProposed` and `myOutcome` are answers about the caller, so the same trial reads differently to the two people in it. A thread the caller is not in answers empty.

post.description: Either side may. The function decides whether they are in the thread and whether it is still live.

patch.description: The other side answers; the one who proposed it cannot confirm their own.
patch.summary: Say yes or no to a time

patch.description: Per side. Both parties answer separately and neither answer overwrites the other — a coach marking a no-show does not put that on the family's record.

get.description: Made or joined, both. `pendingRequests` is zero to anybody but the creator — how many coaches have pitched is the creator's business.

post.description: The creator becomes its first member in the same call — a group of nobody is not a group.

get.description: Readable signed out, because the whole point is that a neighbour can be sent a link and decide. It carries nothing about who is in it, and `alreadyMember` is false for a guest.
get.summary: A group, as an invite link shows it

patch.description: `closed` is a field rather than its own endpoint: it is a creator saying they are done, and it is reversible while the group has not expired.

post.description: Idempotent — joining twice is joining once.

delete.description: The creator cannot: the pitches, the threads and the invite all hang off them, so they close the group instead.

get.description: Each one is also a conversation — the messages are GET /threads/group/{id}/messages.
get.summary: Coaches who have pitched to it

post.description: The creator's decision, and the update policy is what says so.

get.description: `phone` is null unless the group shared one, and `shared` says which kind of null it is — withheld, or simply not on file.

Ordered by distance from the search origin: the given lat/lng if there is one, otherwise the centroid of the area. Only approved, unsuspended coaches, and only in live areas — the area-wise launch gate is the database's, not this endpoint's. Declared before the :id route so /providers/search is not parsed as a coach whose id is the word search.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Search origin. Both or neither; falls back to the area.

get.summary: Coaches near a place, teaching a thing

get.description: Not the public profile: that one is null while a listing is unapproved, so the screen a new coach fills in could never load through it. Field names match the save endpoint so a client can load, edit and send it back unchanged. Null when they have not started one — a real state, not an error. Declared before /:id so it is not read as a coach id.
get.summary: The caller's own listing, as they edit it

put.description: The whole listing, not a patch: branches and service areas are replaced wholesale, so a partial payload would clear what it left out. One transaction — it lands or it does not. A first save leaves the listing waiting for review; an edit does not change approval, so adjusting your fees will not take you out of search.

get.description: Services, fees, branches, the areas they cover, certifications and availability. A coach who is not approved, is suspended, or is an event planner is a 404 — the same answer a stranger gets for an id that was never real.
A coach gets the ones raised with them, a parent gets their own. One endpoint for both sides — the row policy decides which rows those are, so neither has to say who it is.
get.summary: Queries the caller is party to

post.description: One live query per coach — asking twice returns 400 rather than making a second lead. Needs a completed seeker profile and an approved coach, both enforced by the row policy.
post.summary: Ask a coach to get in touch

patch.description: The coach's own queries only. callbackAt is required for callback_scheduled.

post.description: Returns the enquiry to open. If a thread with this family already exists the message lands there instead of starting a second one, and the query is attached to it either way.
post.summary: Reply in writing, opening a conversation
Mark it read, for whichever side is asking

get.description: Public and cached for a few minutes. Fetch once at startup and keep it — these change only when an admin edits the taxonomy or opens an area. Areas are returned whole, with `isLive` alongside: it gates seekers, not providers, so it is a flag and not a filter.
get.summary: Cities, areas and the taxonomy, in one call

get.description: The roster, not the reading surface — GET /feeds/me is what those coaches have been posting. Declared before /:providerId so it is not parsed as a coach called following.

put.description: One reaction per person per post. Send null to clear it; sending the same one again is not a toggle, so a client that wants toggling decides that itself.
put.summary: Like, wow, surprise — or take it back

delete.description: Somebody else's is a 404, because saying 'forbidden' would confirm it exists.

get.description: Readable signed out. iFollow and isMine are answers about the caller, so they are false for a guest. A suspended Space is a 404 to everyone but its owner, and only the owner is told why.
Newest first, so `before` pages backwards. Reaction counts are computed server-side because space_reactions is readable only for your own rows — counting in a client would report one.

post.description: The image is already in Storage; send its public URL as imageUrl. A video carries the 11-character YouTube id and nothing else.

put.description: Idempotent — following twice is following once. Returns the Space as it now reads.

post.description: One message. A coach's first approach is always pending, by check constraint, and stays that way until the family answers — while it does, no second message, no name, no phone number. Writing to the same group twice is refused rather than duplicated.
post.summary: Write to a family, or to a group

get.description: Parents who have written down a requirement, and groups of neighbours who agreed on one together, filtered to what this coach teaches and where they teach it. Untouched rows first, then nearest, then newest. Carries no name, email or phone number: a coach answers through Aspire91 and contact details arrive only if the family shares them.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: The coach's own listing. Must belong to them.

post.description: For a signed-in parent with a stated requirement. search_providers() decides who is eligible; the model only orders them and says why. Answers are cached against a fingerprint of the requirement and the candidate set, so a second look is free until one of them changes. Always returns a list where one exists — `ranked: false` means it is in plain distance order, not that anything failed.
The same idea pointed the other way, over the coach's demand feed. Not cached: unlike the parent's, this one is asked for deliberately rather than rendered on arrival.
post.summary: Families worth a coach's attention first

get.description: Group pitches and direct enquiries in one list. Title, subtitle, unread and iAmSeeker are already resolved for the reader, so the same thread reads differently to the two people in it. threadId is unique within its kind and not across both — pair them for a key.
get.summary: Every conversation the caller is in

get.description: Newest first, so `before` pages backwards. A thread the caller is not party to is an empty list, not a 403 — the row policies decide, and saying 'forbidden' would confirm it exists.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return messages older than this. Pass the createdAt of the oldest you hold.

post.description: The sender is the caller. Bodies are 1 to 4000 characters, which is the database's own constraint stated where a reader can be told about it.
Writes the caller's own read timestamp. Which column that is depends on who they are, which is why it stays a definer function rather than an update the client composes.
post.summary: Mark it read, for whichever side is asking

info.title: Aspire91 API
info.description:
The contract the web app and the Flutter app both speak.

Every request runs against Postgres as the caller, so the row-level security policies in `db/` remain the last word on who may see what. This API adds the contract, the validation and the tests; it does not replace those rules.

tags.name: feeds
tags.description: What coaches have been posting, publicly and per parent

bearer.description: The Supabase access token, exactly as the client SDK issues it.

pendingPitches.description: Coach pitches waiting on a decision, for groups the caller made.

groupsNeedingMembers.description: The caller's groups that are still short of the members to go live.

pendingApproaches.description: Coaches who approached the caller and are waiting on them.

unreadThreads.description: Conversations with something arrived since the caller last looked.

unansweredEnquiries.description: Enquiries a coach has not answered.

unreadQueries.description: Parents who asked to be rung and have not been looked at. Zero for a parent: their own request producing an answer arrives as a thread, which unreadThreads already counts. Clears when the tab is opened, or when the lead moves off 'new' — a coach who has rung somebody has plainly seen it.

needsYou.description: Unread notifications of the kinds that want an action. The bell number, and not the sum of the counters above.

threadId.description: Mark only this conversation's notifications read. Omit to clear everything — which is what opening the bell means.

maxActiveEvents.description: Null is uncapped, 0 grants no event rights.

isDefault.description: What a party of this audience is on before they buy anything.

remaining.description: How many more may be published. Null means no limit.

canPublishAnother.description: Whether another event could be published right now. False on a listing plan with no per-event purchase, which is a coach who has not bought this event yet.

endsOn.description: Null is open-ended — a default plan, or one nobody has put an end date on.

eventId.description: Set for a per-event purchase, which entitles that event and never expires.

maxActiveEvents.description: Omit for uncapped. Zero grants no event rights.
Omit for uncapped. Zero grants no event rights.

paymentStatus.description: Money is a separate axis from attendance, so a late withdrawal can be cancelled without becoming a refund.

amountDue.description: Copied from the category when the entry was made, never read back through it.

cancelledByMe.description: Whether the caller cancelled it themselves, rather than the other side.

participantDob.description: Checked against the category's age range as it will be on the day of the event, which is what an under-10 tournament means.

consentGiven.description: Must be true. The entrant confirms they are the participant, or the participant's parent or guardian consenting to their name and date of birth being held for this event. An entry is the one place this product takes a child's name, so the service records which wording was agreed and when, and refuses the entry without it.

members.description: The rest of a team: the entrant plus these must come to the category's team size. Empty for an individual category.

refund.description: The organiser's call and ignored for anybody else: false cancels the entry without marking a refund due, which is what a non-refundable late withdrawal is.

reference.description: A UPI reference, a cheque number.

teamSize.description: Set for a team, null otherwise.

entriesCount.description: Confirmed entries. A column on the row rather than a count, because RLS hides other families' entries and anything counting as the caller would count only their own.

ownerName.description: The company or coach running it. Null when the owner's row is not visible to this caller, which RLS decides — a public page names who is behind an event, and a page that cannot say is better than one that guesses.

bookingMode.description: Stated, never inferred from whether externalBookingUrl is set: platform takes entries here, external sends them to the organiser's own site, none is an announcement.

cancellationDeadline.description: After this a family can no longer withdraw itself. Falls back to bookingClosesAt and then to startsAt; its own column because 'no withdrawals in the last week' cannot be expressed by closing entries a week early.
Leave unset and a family may withdraw until entries close.
Leave unset and a family may withdraw until entries close.

id.description: The row this replaces. Present means edit that category, absent means add one — which is what lets a category keep its id, and therefore its entries, across a save.

coachCount.description: Approved coaches serving a live area of this city.

youtubeId.description: The 11-character YouTube id. Set when kind is video.

myReaction.description: This caller's own reaction. Absent on the public feed, which has no caller.

iReported.description: Whether this caller has already reported it.

reason.description: Why this post is in the feed. 'following' means the caller follows this coach; 'interest' means we suggested them. Absent on the public feed.

role.description: Only settable while the account has no role. Changing an existing one is switch_role's job, which refuses once a profile is complete and clears up what is left behind.

lookingFor.description: Service category ids they said they are looking for. Empty until they say.

id.description: The listing id, which is not the user id.

approved.description: Visible in search. False means waiting on an admin.

isSuspended.description: Taken down. Different from never approved, and says so.

role.description: Null when the account exists but no role has been chosen. organiser was missing from this list while profiles.role has allowed it since 3E — harmless to a client reading a string, and a deserialisation failure for one generating an enum.

profileComplete.description: Whether they finished the profile their role requires.

seeker.description: Present only for a seeker. Null when the role is set but the row is not.

phone.description: Digits, optionally with +, spaces or hyphens. Stored as written.

officeAddress.description: Where the company is, not where its events are. A venue is asked for per event, since an organiser runs each one somewhere different.

approved.description: Visible publicly. False means waiting on an admin.

isSuspended.description: Taken down. Different from never approved, and says so.

relationToLearner.description: Who they are looking for. A fact about the person rather than the search — a father is a father whether or not he is looking this month — and it changes what a coach is being asked to do.

openToOffers.description: The consent switch, and nothing else here reads as one. Off hides them from students_for_provider entirely and immediately.

marketingOptIn.description: Asked in plain words, and defaulted off.

requirementUpdatedAt.description: Stamped on every save: the demand feed sorts on it.

profileComplete.description: Whether the profile has ever been saved in full.

areaId.description: Where they are. This is what search is centred on.

openToOffers.description: Whether coaches may approach them. Defaults true because a parent who has just typed out what they want has, in the ordinary meaning of it, asked to be found.

marketingOptIn.description: Defaulted off, and asked in plain words.

providerId.description: The coach being written to. Must be approved.

serviceCategoryId.description: What they are asking about. Optional: a parent may just want to talk, and forcing a taxonomy pick before the first message is friction at exactly the wrong moment.

message.description: A coach is judging a stranger on this, so there is a floor.

sharePhone.description: Whether the coach may see this family's number. Opt in, never a default, and per enquiry rather than per account: sharing it with one coach is not sharing it with every coach who ever writes.

accept.description: True opens the conversation, false declines it.

askedAt.description: When they asked, not when the coach replied.

kind.description: Which surface the conversation belongs to. It decides where the messages live and which actions the thread offers, so a client must branch on it.

threadId.description: The group request or the enquiry. Unique within its kind, not across both — pair it with kind before using it as a key.

status.description: Where the approach or enquiry stands.

initiatedBy.description: Who opened it. A group pitch is always the coach's approach.

unread.description: Something arrived after this reader last looked, and they did not send it. Computed for the caller, so it means different things to the two sides of the same thread.

iAmSeeker.description: Which side of this conversation the caller is on.

showPhone.description: Whether this family's number is shared with the coach. Null on a group thread, which has no such switch. Opt in and revocable, per conversation rather than per account — sharing a number with one coach is not sharing it with every coach who writes.

origin.description: Set when this conversation began with a request for a call. A message from somebody you never wrote to is what makes contact feel unsolicited, so the parent is told which of their own requests produced it. Null for every other thread.

share.description: Revocable on purpose. A parent who shared a number and then thought better of it can take it back, and the contact endpoints stop answering immediately.

place.description: A teaching place id, not a uuid.

studentCount.description: For a group, how many are coming.

iProposed.description: Whether the caller is the one who suggested it.

myOutcome.description: Whichever of the two above belongs to the caller. Both sides record what happened separately, so neither is asked to accept the other's account of it.

threadId.description: The conversation this is being arranged in.

placeNote.description: Directions, a landmark, a gate number.

studentCount.description: For a group thread: how many children are coming.

societyName.description: Identifying detail. Never shown to anybody outside the group.

studentCount.description: How many children the group is asking for.

expiresAt.description: Time-boxed on purpose: stale demand costs a coach's trust faster than none.

isActive.description: Open, unexpired, and with enough families to be worth pitching to.

pendingRequests.description: Coaches waiting on an answer. Zero to anybody but the creator.

societyName.description: The society or building. Identifying, so it is never shown outside the group — but it is the thing that makes neighbours recognise their own group.

sharePhone.description: Opt in, never a default. This is a parent's personal number.

validityDays.description: How long it runs for. Groups are time-boxed because stale demand costs a coach's trust faster than no demand does, and the creator picks the window rather than taking the column default.

isOpen.description: Whether it can still be joined.

alreadyMember.description: Whether the caller is already in it. False when signed out.

sharePhone.description: Whether coaches may see the group's number.

closed.description: True stops coaches pitching. Setting it false reopens the group — and pushes the expiry out if it had already lapsed, because clearing closed_at alone would leave a group that says it is open and that nobody can pitch to.

extend.description: True pushes the expiry 10 days out from now. Groups are time-boxed because stale demand costs a coach's trust faster than no demand does, so this is the creator saying it is still wanted rather than a date they pick.

pitch.description: What they wrote to the group.

isCreator.description: Whether the caller made the group this was pitched to.

shared.description: Whether the group is sharing a number at all.

helpStatement.description: What they say they can help with.

teachingPlaces.description: Where they teach — own centre, at home, online.

year.description: Kept as text: parents write '2019' and 'expected 2027' alike.

place.description: Which of the coach's teaching places this slot is at.

approved.description: False until an admin has read it. Not the caller's to change.

isSuspended.description: Taken down. Different from never approved.

profileComplete.description: Whether the listing has ever been saved in full.

year.description: Text, because coaches write '2019' and 'expected 2027' alike.

place.description: Which teaching place this slot is at.

areaId.description: Where it is. This is what makes it findable.

branches.description: Institutions only. Cleared for anybody else, so a change of type is not half a listing.

serviceAreaIds.description: Individuals only. The areas they will travel to or teach in.

approved.description: False until an admin reads the listing. A first save is always false.

isSuspended.description: Taken down. Different from never approved, and says so.

group.description: Which taxonomy group it belongs to — sport, subject, and so on.

helpStatement.description: What they say they can help with.

teachingPlaces.description: Where they teach — at their centre, at home, online.

providerName.description: The coach's name, for the parent's list.

contactName.description: As given when the query was raised, not as the profile reads now.

contactPhone.description: Only ever visible to the two parties.

enquiryId.description: The conversation this query produced, once one exists.

unread.description: Whether the caller has looked at this one. mark_query_read() has existed since phase3h and nothing ever called it, because no field here said there was anything to mark — so a coach had a read column that never went true and no badge that could have used it.

providerId.description: The coach being asked. Must be approved.

contactPhone.description: Required, unlike on an enquiry. The point of a query is to be called, so one without a number is a request nobody can act on. Prefilled from the profile and editable, so a second number can be used without changing the account.

callbackAt.description: Required when status is callback_scheduled, ignored otherwise.

enquiryId.description: The conversation to open. An existing thread with this family if there was one, so a parent never ends up with two conversations for one coach.

isLive.description: Open to seekers. Providers may register in an area before it opens, so this is a flag rather than a filter — the seeker-facing screens honour it, signup does not.

group.description: One of the eight taxonomy groups. Drives the colour a category renders in.

id.description: A short text id, not a uuid.

reaction.description: Null clears the caller's reaction. Sending the same one again is not a toggle.

iFollow.description: Whether the caller follows it. False when signed out.

suspendedReason.description: Why it was taken down. The owner's business and nobody else's, so null to them.

isHidden.description: A hidden post stays in the table — the report queue is about it, and deleting the evidence when the complaint arrives is the wrong instinct. Only the owner sees one.

myReaction.description: The caller's own. Counted server-side: space_reactions is readable only for your own rows.

imageUrl.description: Storage URL for a photo post. The database refuses anything not http(s).

providerId.description: The coach's own listing. Must belong to them.

message.description: The pitch. Twenty characters is the database's own floor for a group request and the web's for both — a family judges a stranger on this, and three words is not enough to judge on.

serviceCategoryId.description: Which service this is about. Ignored for a group, which already names one.

id.description: The enquiry or the group request.

status.description: Always 'pending' for a coach's first message. The family decides what follows.

id.description: The seeker or the group. Unique within its kind.

serviceNames.description: The service names, as they read today.

serviceGroups.description: Which taxonomy groups those services sit in.

distanceKm.description: Kilometres from the nearest place this coach can be found at.

learnerAge.description: The learner's age. Never their name.

preferredModes.description: At home, at your centre, online.

studentCount.description: How many children this is for.

memberCount.description: Families in the group. 1 for a single parent's requirement.

expiresAt.description: When a group stops accepting answers. Null for a single requirement.

contactStatus.description: Set once this coach has written to them, and null until. Rows with a status are pushed below the untouched ones and are not re-ranked by the suggestions endpoint.

provider.description: Exactly what GET /providers/search returns for a coach — same eighteen fields, same camelCase, and the same schema in the generated contract.

reason.description: Why the model placed this coach here. Null when the list was not ranked.

ranked.description: False when the list is in plain distance order.

cached.description: True when served from the stored ranking.

reason.description: Why there is nothing to show; absent when there is. The caller renders these very differently — 'no_requirement' is an invitation to state one, 'not_a_seeker' is not.

providerId.description: The coach's own listing. Must belong to them.

reason.description: Why the model placed it here.
Why there is nothing to rank. 'no_demand' also covers too few untouched rows to be worth a model call — the caller keeps showing its own unranked list either way.

threadId.description: The group request or enquiry this belongs to.

body.description: The ceiling is the database's own check constraint, repeated here so an over-long message is a sentence about length rather than a constraint violation.
